readings.title: Redemption of Property
readings.subtitle: Land, Houses, and the Levites
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:24] <dq>‘And in all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption of the land.</dq> [25] <dq>‘When your brother becomes poor and has sold some of his possession, and his redeemer, a close relative, comes to redeem it, then he shall redeem what his brother sold.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And when the man has no one to redeem it, but he himself becomes able to redeem it,</dq> [27] <dq>then he shall calculate the years since its sale, and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, that he might return to his possession.</dq> [28] <dq>‘But if he is not able to get it back for himself, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the Year of Jubilee. And it shall be released in the Jubilee, and he shall return to his possession.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then his right of redemption shall be at the end of a year after it is sold. For a full year he has the right of redemption.</dq> [30] <dq>‘But if it is not redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house in the walled city shall belong to him who bought it, throughout his generations. It is not released in the Jubilee.</dq> [31] <dq>‘However, the houses of villages which have no wall around them shall be reckoned as the fields of the country. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.</dq> [32] <dq>‘As for the cities of the Lewites, and the houses in the cities of their possession, the Lewites have a right of redemption forever.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And if a man purchases a house from the Lewites, then the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall be released in the Jubilee, for the houses in the cities of the Lewites are their possession among the children of Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [34] <dq>‘But the field of the open land of their cities is not sold, for it is their everlasting possession.</dq>

readings.title: Treatment of the Poor and Servants
readings.subtitle: Laws of Lending and Servitude
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:35] <dq>‘And when your brother becomes poor, and his hand has failed with you, then you shall sustain him, and he shall live with you, like a stranger or a sojourner.</dq> [36] <dq>‘Take no interest from him, or profit, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and your brother shall live with you.</dq> [37] <dq>‘Do not lend him your silver on interest, and do not lend him your food for profit.</dq> [38] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you the land of Kena’an, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And when your brother becomes poor with you, and has sold himself to you, do not make him serve as a slave.</dq> [40] <dq>‘As a hired servant, as a sojourner, he is with you, he serves you until the Year of Jubilee.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And he shall leave you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own clan, even return to the possession of his fathers.</dq> [42] <dq>‘For they are <dn>My</dn> servants, whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim, they are not sold as slaves.</dq> [43] <dq>‘Do not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And your male and female slaves whom you have, from the nations that are around you, from them you buy male and female slaves.</dq> [45] <dq>‘And also of the children of the strangers who sojourn among you, from them you might buy, and of their clans who are with you, which they brought forth in your land, and they shall be your property.</dq> [46] <dq>‘And you can leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit them as a possession, they are your slaves for all time. But as for your brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl, you shall not rule over one another with harshness.</dq> [47] <dq>‘And when a sojourner or a stranger with you becomes rich, and your brother with him becomes poor, and sells himself to the sojourner or stranger with you, or to a member of the stranger’s clan,</dq> [48] <dq>after he has been sold, he has right of redemption, one of his brothers redeems him,</dq> [49] <dq>or his uncle or his uncle’s son redeems him, or anyone who is near of kin to him in his clan redeems him, or if he is able, then he shall redeem himself.</dq> [50] <dq>‘And he shall reckon with him who bought him: The price of his release shall be according to the number of years, from the year that he was sold to him until the Year of Jubilee, according to the days of a hired servant it is with him.</dq> [51] <dq>‘If there are yet many years, according to them he repays the price of his redemption from the silver of his purchase.</dq> [52] <dq>‘And if there remain but few years until the Year of Jubilee, then he shall reckon with him, and according to his years he repays him the price of his redemption.</dq> [53] <dq>‘He shall be with him as a yearly hired servant, and he shall not rule with harshness over him in your eyes.</dq> [54] <dq>‘And if he is not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the Year of Jubilee, he and his children with him.</dq> [55] <dq>‘For the children of Yisra’ĕl are servants to <dn>Me</dn>, they are <dn>My</dn> servants whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Blessings for Obedience
readings.subtitle: Rain, Peace, and Divine Presence
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:1] <dq>‘Do not make idols for yourselves, and do not set up a carved image or a pillar for yourselves, and do not place a stone image in your land, to bow down to it. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [2] <dq>‘Guard <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths and reverence <dn>My</dn> set-apart place. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘If you walk in <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>My</dn> commands, and shall do them,</dq> [4] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the field yield their fruit.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And your threshing shall reach to the grape harvest, and the grape harvest reach to the sowing time, and you shall eat your bread to satisfaction, and dwell in your land safely.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall give peace in the land, and you shall lie down and no one make you afraid. And <dn>I</dn> shall clear the land of evil beasts, and not let the sword go through your land.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you pursue ten thousand. And your enemies shall fall by the sword before you.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall turn to you and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and establish <dn>My</dn> covenant with you.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall eat the old crop, and clear out the old because of the new.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> Dwelling Place in your midst, and <dn>My</dn> being shall not loathe you.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall walk in your midst, and shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall be <dn>My</dn> people.</dq> [13] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from being their slaves. And <dn>I</dn> have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.</dq>

readings.title: Penalties for Disobedience
readings.subtitle: The Curse of the Broken Covenant
readings.text: [Leviticus 26:14] <dq>‘But if you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, and do not do all these commands,</dq> [15] <dq>and if you reject <dn>My</dn> laws, or if your being loathes <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, so that you do not do all <dn>My</dn> commands, but break <dn>My</dn> covenant,</dq> [16] <dq><dn>I</dn> also do this to you: And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint sudden terror over you, wasting disease and inflammation that dim the eyes and cause the being to pine away. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against you, and you shall be smitten before your enemies. And those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And if after this you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, then <dn>I</dn> shall punish you seven times more for your sins.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall break the pride of your power, and shall make your heavens like iron and your earth like bronze.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And your strength shall be spent in vain, for your land shall not yield its produce, nor the trees of the land yield their fruit.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And if you walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>, and refuse to obey <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall bring on you seven times more plagues, according to your sins,</dq> [22] <dq>and send wild beasts among you, which shall bereave you of your children, and cut off your livestock, and make you few in number, and your highways shall be laid waste.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And if you are not disciplined by <dn>Me</dn> in these, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [24] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> also shall walk contrary to you, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall smite you seven times for your sins.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall bring against you a sword executing the vengeance of the covenant, and when you are gathered together within your cities <dn>I</dn> shall send pestilence among you, and you shall be given into the hand of the enemy.</dq> [26] <dq>‘When <dn>I</dn> have cut off your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall bring back your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if in spite of this you do not obey <dn>Me</dn>, but walk contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [28] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall walk contrary to you in wrath. And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall punish you seven times for your sins.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and eat the flesh of your daughters.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall destroy your high places, and cut down your sun-pillars, and put your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols. And <dn>My</dn> being shall loathe you.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall lay your cities waste and bring your set-apart places to desolation, and not smell your sweet fragrances.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall lay the land waste, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished at it.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter you among the gentiles and draw out a sword after you. And your land shall be waste and your cities laid waste.</dq> [34] <dq>‘Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies waste and you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land shall rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.</dq> [35] <dq>‘As long as it lies waste it rests, for the time it did not rest on your Sabbaths when you dwelt in it.</dq> [36] <dq>‘And as for those of you who are left, <dn>I</dn> shall send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a shaken leaf shall cause them to flee. And they shall flee as fleeing from a sword, and they shall fall when no one pursues.</dq> [37] <dq>‘And they shall stumble over one another, as before a sword, when no one pursues. And you shall be unable to stand before your enemies.</dq> [38] <dq>‘And you shall perish among the gentiles, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And those of you who are left shall rot away in their crookedness in your enemies’ lands, and also in the crookedness of their fathers they shall rot away with them.</dq> [40] <dq>‘But if they confess their crookedness and the crookedness of their fathers, with their trespass in which they trespassed against <dn>Me</dn>, and that they also have walked contrary to <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [41] <dq>and that <dn>I</dn> also have walked contrary to them and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if their uncircumcised heart is then humbled, and they accept the punishment of their crookedness,</dq> [42] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>My</dn> covenant with Ya’aqoḇ, and also <dn>My</dn> covenant with Yitsḥaq, and also <dn>My</dn> covenant with Aḇraham <dn>I</dn> remember, and <dn>I</dn> remember the land.</dq> [43] <dq>‘For the land was left by them, and enjoyed its Sabbaths while it lay waste without them. And they were accepting the punishment of their crookedness, because they despised <dn>My</dn> right-rulings and because their being loathed <dn>My</dn> laws.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And yet for all this, when they are in the land of their enemies, <dn>I</dn> shall not reject them, nor shall <dn>I</dn> loathe them so as to destroy them and break <dn>My</dn> covenant with them. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [45] <dq>‘Then <dn>I</dn> shall remember for their sake the covenant of the ancestors, whom <dn>I</dn> brought out of the land of Mitsrayim in the sight of the gentiles to be their <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [46] These are the laws and the right-rulings and the Toroth which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made between <dn>Himself</dn> and the children of Yisra’ĕl on Mount Sinai by the hand of Mosheh.
